intro:
The CAG page-brief audit (https://claude.ai/artifact/S5xqdrrgFmmgcWFuuoqTGN) found 25 gaps to close
before project 5. Two of them change what the pages look like, so they are yours to pick. The
plan builds the recommended option unless you pick otherwise. Claude's recommendation is marked.

questions.context: CAG renders every in-body photo and infographic in one box: 760px wide at 16:9, with portraits full-bleed at 4:5 on phones. BSUK's rebuilt pages use `.bl-img`: full width, capped at 420px from 900px up, at the photo's own ratio. Working rule 17 puts an image under every heading on 30+ new pages. Recommended: (a) — a fixed box cannot shift the layout while images load, and it lets the "image first under every H3" check actually find the images (today it matches nothing). Trade-off: the 12 built pages keep `.bl-img` until they are next touched.

options.label: CAG's uniform box on new pages (760px, 16:9; portrait 4:5 full-bleed on phones)

questions.question: What box should in-body images use on the new city, comparison and blog pages?
questions.where: CAG brief §15a; plan Task 8; the kit image CSS.

questions.context: 12 of the 13 approved boards set `global_cta` to hidden, but the footer always shows the band, so those built pages do not match what you approved. Recommended: (a) — build what was approved. Trade-off: the band disappears from the 12 built pages that chose hidden (each keeps its own in-page CTA).

options.label: Wire it: "hidden" hides the band on that page
Retire the setting: the band shows on every page and boards stop asking

questions.question: Should the footer's "Ready to meet the litter?" band obey the board's global CTA setting?

title: CAG parity · two decisions before project 5
